Endhuvi (Endhuvi, R36)

Region (English scoring-table region): Rahen.

In one sentence: A riverine Harimari state in Rahen uses debate, porcelain, and river-spirit belief to find another order within and beyond a weakening Raj system.

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 53/100 | Authoritarianism 45/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 96/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 84/100) | Pluralism 82/100. The v2.1 value is Good (79/100), with an improving trajectory. Mobile countryside education, peaceful negotiation, sharing the river's gifts with other peoples, and urban repair have clear public-benefit evidence; caste and monarchy remain at the starting point, while later expansion and spirit competition also involve coercion, so this is not an unconditional perfect score.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Medium-long (42 direct R36 definitions, including hidden phases) | Verified version: local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: High | Grind: Medium-high (subject politics, religious conversion, and river crisis) | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion: Medium

A river and a small country

Endhuvi already exists in 1444 as a Harimari-ruled state of Rahen, with its capital in the Kharunyana basin. Local history sets it as a kingdom with a caste system, following High Philosophy, and opening with King Vapyatar VI; it has an old rivalry with R49. It is not merely a small country sitting at the Raj's edge waiting to be absorbed: river transport, the Porcelain City, forts, and an attentive view of high politics give it leverage to escape the status quo. No independently verifiable Endhuvi main page was found in the offline English Wiki; the country's prehistory therefore rests mainly on the current Mod.

The rivalry has a concrete origin. The native idea text says that after Phoenix Emperor Jaerel died in 1136, the states of Rahen fought over land, and Endhuvi and Parusad Bhola repeatedly contested the fertile plains of Maharaaja. In 1306, Ramapalar the Reunifier conquered Dhujat and divided the disputed land between both sides and the Royal court, leaving an unsatisfactory three-way settlement. Waiting and watching consequently became part of Endhuvi's self-narrative. This is opening history in the idea text, not proof that the player has already recovered the plain. The related Mystic Accord Wiki entry describes the great spirit of the Kharunyana as a white catfish; that supplies religious worldbuilding, not evidence that Endhuvi had converted or already seen the river spirit in 1444.

The early tree manages two things at once. Externally, it repairs relations through river trade, porcelain artisans, and negotiation; internally, it recognizes the Cinnabar Lotus Society, founded by young thinkers, and expands teahouse arguments into formal debate, education for the ruler, and travelling countryside schools. Official development material says that this line undergoes two religious upheavals while looking for an exit from the Raj's rigid institutions. The “Ruby Garden Debate” is both negotiation and a political effort to win independence with allied support. Endhuvi is less a country that conquers the world by the sword than one that gives its ideas power first, then fights for territory on their behalf.

This reform is not confined to court. Mission text proposes putting small schools on boats and sending them down Kharunyana tributaries to remote villages, giving people previously excluded from scholarly circles access to education. Porcelain artisans and river merchants provide revenue and connections, making “debate” a question of who benefits from trade and knowledge flows rather than abstract philosophy alone. For the personality model, these concrete measures matter more than the phrase “enlightened king.”

From debate to the river's source

The abnormal flow of the Kharunyana, floods, and river creatures turn philosophical questions into survival questions. Mages, monks, and thinkers explain the crisis, while friends in the Mystic Accord propose that the river itself is a great spirit; eventually the river spirit appears as a gigantic catfish. The missions can turn Endhuvi toward new practice and spirit relations, drawing temples, headwaters, and the whole basin into state-building. Later goals include porcelain trade, river defence, reaching the source, and confronting nearby spirits. The fish is not a joke reward: it symbolizes a route that joins knowledge, belief, and geography.

After the turn toward spirits, Endhuvi does not abandon debate. Instead it raises the question of whether the river has consciousness and how it should be treated to the national level; water once explained separately by mages, monks, and merchants becomes a new public faith. The border extends from the banks to the headwaters, and a waterway policy that began defensively can become a reason for regional expansion. Its openness and potential coercion meet here: it is willing to share the river's bounty, but also wants other rivers and spirits to accept its interpretation.

The mission text also offers a fork: restore the name and ambitions of ancient Great Dhujat, or continue along Endhuvi's own river path. These are not two successor trees automatically added together; the current entry counts only R36's 42 direct missions. The personality card calls it Good because rural education, peaceful negotiation, and sharing the river's gifts with other peoples are positive evidence, while the caste-based starting point, expansion, and competition among spirits and powers mean it is not a coercion-free utopia. Community discussion generally treats it as an unusual porcelain-and-spirit campaign, but the exact difficulty of a guide changes with version.

Endhuvi suits players who like small-country diplomacy, intellectual debate, religious turns, river economies, and mysticism. Players who want an immediately clear conquest route may find the hidden phases and subject politics too slow. Its future is a set of mission possibilities, not a completed 1444 independence, religious conversion, or spirit manifestation.

Its distinctive quality is not “choose peace and never fight.” Every step outward brings a new society, belief, or stretch of river back to the debate table. That is why Endhuvi is neither an ordinary trade minor nor an ordinary spirit state.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces native English national-idea names and descriptions alongside the inherited source displays. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not stack automatically with the predecessor set. Descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal, not events already completed in 1444. Native English prose is used rather than back-translating the Chinese localisation; any inherited display/unit uncertainty remains unresolved.

Endhuvi (R36) — Endhuvi Ideas

Traditions: Endhuvi Traditions

Idea 1: Sentinels of Phangban Crossing

The great Bom city of Phangban sits just beyond the river-sea Kharunyana, her lights visible from Endhuvi, faintly glittering on the water at night. Here, the river slows and meanders, becoming shallow enough that a great bridge was erected in ancient times. This bridge connects the two distant shores of the river with the holy island of Fenglan and the high temple that takes up most of its area.

As one of only a few places where one can easily cross from Bomdan into Rahen, this site holds critical importance to the Raj, and it has long been the duty of the Senapti of the East to hold this crossing against all foreign incursions - and to be ready to sally forth and lead the armies of the Raja across the river against the kingdoms of the Bom.

Effects: Fort defensiveness: +15%.

Idea 2: Merchants of the Porcelain River

South of Semphrerong and Sarisung but north of Khiraspid and Sramaya, Endhuvi sits at the heart of the great flow of trade that bobs along the Kharunyana. Countless barges come and go through the Endhuvi shallows, loading and unloading goods at her markets before departing again.

While many merchants prefer to trade in cosmopolitan Phangban, the city is crowded and it can be difficult to conduct deals that one would rather have no witnesses or competition for. The quieter shallows of Endhuvi, with their many small harbors and coves, offer that alternative market, and great wealth flows into her coffers despite the greater wealth that concentrates in Phangban.

Effects: Trade efficiency: +10%.

Idea 3: Philosopher Evangelists of Rahen

Countless people travel through Endhuvi - up and down the Kharunyana, west from Bomdan and Xianjie, east from Bulwar and Sarhal. To all of them we have posed the great questions that have confounded our philosopher-kings since time immemorial, and we have found them all wanting, their understanding of rhetoric and epistemology sorely underdeveloped.

This cannot be blamed on the outsiders, however, for they have not been steeped in the culture of the world's greatest civilization since their births. In Endhuvi, every child learns the proper ways to speak, to act, and to think. Clearly this is not the way of the rest of the world, but like a child must be guided, so too must we gently educate all those who come to these lands in proper thought and practice, so that one day all the world will be worthy to sit and debate the wisdom of the High Gods.

Effects: Accepted cultures: +2.

Idea 4: Long Struggle for Maharaaja

The death of Phoenix Emperor Jaerel in 1136 AA sent Rahen into chaos, with myriad petty kingdoms descending into war over territorial disputes. One such dispute was our ancient and rightful claim to the fertile plains of Maharaaja, contested between ourselves and the neighboring princes of Parusad Bhola. The territory traded hands a dozen times until Ramapalar the Reunifier conquered Dhujat in 1306 AA. The great Raja settled the dispute by splitting the land equally betwen ourselves, our ancient rivals, and the Royal throne.

For many years this dissatisfactory status quo held, with verdant Maharaaja split in three, and Endhuvi waited, patient, for her opportunity to finally take her rightful land. In many ways, the waiting came to be more important than the land itself - for while the plains would eventually be reclaimed, fought over, and lost again, the standoff would come to characterise the Rasarhid people of Endhuvi. Phrases like 'stoic as a Rasarhid' or 'waiting on Maharaaja' entered the lexicon of the many tongues of Rahen, so great was the reputation of the folk of Endhuvi.

Effects: Aggressive expansion impact: -10%.

Idea 5: The Cinnabar Lotus Debate Society

None of its original six members expected the Cinnabar Lotus Society to grow into a famous organization. Meeting for the first time in 1546, the informal debate society quickly garnered a major following among progressive scholars, and the gatherings of the group rapidly grew so large that no meeting hall could hold them.

Forced to relocate to a series of barges on the Kharunyana to accommodate its balooning attendance, the size of the floating meeting hall of the Cinnabar Lotus would continue to grow over the next decade. Soon known far and wide as a great hub of thinkers, the Cinnabar Lotus was second only to the Hall of Endless Debate in its prestige among Raheni scholars, and famous members of the society such as Agnimitra of the Iron Way and Vishwanath Andipalar Malviya produced some of the most fascinating treatises on moral philosophy and theology that had ever been seen in Haless.

Effects: Idea cost: -10%.

Idea 6: The Darasar Rearguard

In 1572 AA, the Hobgoblin Legion took a plunge into the heart of Dhugajir and began the fifteen-year conflict known as the Great Dhujat War. In a slow but inexorable advance The Command marched south, sieging the great fortresses of Dhujat and strangling resistance in the countryside. When their eastern column came to Endhuvi, Senapti Ghirakhur of the Shadow Claw abandoned the indefensible city and took 7000 of his best fighters into the dense jungles to wage a guerrila war against the hobgoblins.

In a military campaign that would come to be known as 'The Darasar Rearguard', Senapti Ghirakur and his 7000 clashed with the forces of The Command in brutal jungle warfare and lightning raids, disrupting lines of supply and communication before fading away into the wild thickets. The efforts of Ghirakhur's 7000 are considered instrumental in preventing the Command from completing the Siege of Khiraspid, and to this day are the proudest moment in Endhuvi's military history.

Effects: Hostile attrition: +100%; Army tradition from battles: +0.5.

Idea 7: Shoal of Great Spirit Kharunyana

The Great Dhujat War brought ruin not only to the farms and cities, but upon the High Temples themselves. This sacrilege would bring about a much greater change in Dhujat than any could have predicted at the war's beginning - for without the soothing presence of the High Temples, the spirits of Haless stirred once more.

One rainy morning in 1593, an earthquake struck near Endhuvi. The cause was soon made apparent when an enormous catfish, its scales glittering every color of the rainbow, emerged from the mud of the river, its tail-strikes shaking the earth. The magical creature was seemingly non-hostile, and folk flocked to the shore to get a glimpse of the vast beast.

The spirit fish would eventually disappear into the vastness of the river-sea, but returned to the shallows of Endhuvi often. Many took the gentle spirit's favoritism of their waters as a sign of good luck, and whenever the spirit returned festivals would be thrown celebrating its presence. In later times the Spirit Fish would become a symbol of Endhuvi, and its majesty the primary reason foreigners visited the city.

Effects: National unrest: -2.
